rows.source: HSE young-people-at-work guidance
rows.verified: Employers have the same health, safety and welfare responsibilities for workers under 18 as for other workers.

rows.source: HSE young-people-at-work guidance
rows.verified: Young people can be at greater risk during the first six months of work because the workplace and its risks are unfamiliar.

rows.source: HSE young-people-at-work guidance
rows.verified: Risk assessments should be reviewed before employing a young person for the first time or where the young person has particular needs.

rows.source: HSE young-people-at-work guidance
rows.verified: Relevant factors include inexperience, limited maturity, incomplete physical development, eagerness to impress and uncertainty about raising concerns.

rows.source: HSE young-people-at-work guidance
rows.verified: Higher-risk work requires careful consideration of the tasks, hazards, controls, instruction, training and supervision.

rows.source: HSE young-people-at-work guidance
rows.verified: Additional considerations can include radiation, noise, vibration, toxic substances and extreme temperatures.

rows.source: HSE young-people-at-work guidance
rows.verified: Young people need clear and sufficient instruction, training and supervision, with checks that they understood the hazards and precautions.

rows.source: HSE young-people-at-work guidance
rows.verified: Young workers often need more supervision than adults and age limits may be appropriate for some equipment and machinery.

rows.source: HSE young-people-at-work guidance
rows.verified: Young-worker risk depends on age, maturity, experience, physical development, task, environment, training comprehension, supervision and equipment restrictions.

rows.source: HSE young-people-at-work guidance
rows.verified: General additional risk factors, assessment, instruction, training, supervision and age restrictions guidance does not prove the current condition, exposure or control performance at an individual parcel and does not establish an exact event or illness probability.

rows.source: HSE migrant-worker health and safety guidance
rows.verified: All workers are protected by British health and safety law regardless of whether they are working in Great Britain legally.

rows.source: HSE migrant-worker health and safety guidance
rows.verified: Every worker has the right to a workplace where health and safety risks are properly controlled.

rows.source: HSE migrant-worker health and safety guidance
rows.verified: Employers have the same health and safety responsibilities for migrant workers as for British workers.

rows.source: HSE migrant-worker health and safety guidance
rows.verified: Employers must explain job-related risks and the precautions taken to protect workers.

rows.source: HSE migrant-worker health and safety guidance
rows.verified: Employers must provide the information, instruction and training needed for safe work and check that it is understood.

rows.source: HSE migrant-worker health and safety guidance
rows.verified: Workers must use machinery and safety equipment as trained and report unsafe conditions or unsafe work.

rows.source: HSE migrant-worker health and safety guidance
rows.verified: Unresolved safety concerns can be raised with HSE confidentially without the worker having to provide their name.

rows.source: HSE migrant-worker health and safety guidance
rows.verified: A worker is not required to disclose disability or pregnancy details, but an employer cannot take necessary protective action without relevant information.

rows.source: HSE migrant-worker health and safety guidance
rows.verified: Migrant-worker risk depends on task, employment arrangements, language and literacy, training comprehension, supervision, accommodation, transport and ability to raise concerns.

rows.source: HSE migrant-worker health and safety guidance
rows.verified: General equal protection, employer communication and training, worker duties and confidential concern reporting guidance does not prove the current condition, exposure or control performance at an individual parcel and does not establish an exact event or illness probability.
